newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Gold seen under pressure in Europe, trade brisk.
newsitem.headline: Gold seen under pressure in Europe, trade brisk.

text.p: Precious metals opened Monday mostly easier in brisk trading on the last day of the semester, and dealers said the market could face fresh selling pressure after touching four-year lows last week.
"You have to be cautious today. Gold is still under pressure, and after hitting the year's lows I think we'll go lower. Testing $332 is certainly possible," one dealer said.
Gold opened at $334.60/$335.00 an ounce, down from $336.90/$337.40 at the London close on Friday.
Another dealer said he expected gold to stay in a range of $333/$336 today, with a generally weaker tone.
Silver eased four cents to $4.69/$4.71, following gold.

"Silver is still wedged in its range, but I wonder how long this can last given gold's weakness," one Swiss dealer said. "I think $4.65 has to hold and we have to close abover this level or we will head lower."

Platinum firmed to $419.00/$422.00 from $416.00/$421.00 as jitters about Russian deliveries propped up prices. "We are still waiting for Godot," one dealer quipped, referring to the long wait for confirmation supplies were reaching the market.
